title: Minimax Testing of Risk-Difference Homogeneity across Sparse Strata with Uncertain Propensities
banked_reason: Math referee PASS; whole-paper tier subfield, paper_score_ceiling 6.6 < field threshold 7.4, salvageable=false; the all-parameter matched width frontier remains open.
gap_reasons: The proposal's all-parameter directly evaluable matched frontier is still an open question; the delivered bracket and regional matched rates are a weaker kernel and must be positioned as the note's actual contribution rather than its promised completion.

Position this regional homogeneity-testing rate theorem against accepted-bank stat_discrete_ate_heterogeneity_frontier: it is distinct (ATE estimation under bounded heterogeneity versus testing energy-separated alternatives) but is close enough to require an explicit relevance-and-difference sentence.
The requested universal width characterization remains unresolved: at eta=Delta with fixed Delta<=1/64 and growing K, the delivered bounds still span sqrt(K)/Delta^2 to K^(3/4)/Delta.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved a global rate bracket, total finite original-record tests calibrated over the full unknown-common-effect null, and matching all-test rates in balanced, dense, and broad-width regions. Two maximality improvements extended the pair and axis-mixture regions, but the all-parameter matched width frontier remains open. The math referee passed; the whole-paper score ceiling was 6.6 below the field threshold 7.4, so the run was banked downgraded at subfield without entering formalization.
tldr: Risk-difference homogeneity allows every stratum to share an unknown nonzero effect. On known-uniform sparse strata with binary arm means in \([1/4,3/4]\) and a public propensity interval centered at one half, the note proves original-record tests and same-class all-test converses. The rate is \(R_2\) in the balanced and dense regions proved by the pair and endpoint results, and \(U\) in the broad-width region proved by the axis-mixture result. A gap-calibrated pair rule applies whenever \(\eta<\Delta/2\). A matched formula over all remaining public parameters is still requested by \texttt{oeq:complete-width-frontier}; its transitions and any logarithmic factors are unresolved. Sparse risk-difference tests, subgroup U-tests, and structured-CATE homogeneity methods are direct predecessors. Priority remains conditional on the inaccessible published theorem texts of the older sparse-homogeneity papers.
gap: Park and Gauran directly study sparse risk-difference homogeneity; only their published abstract is verified, so its theorem-level frontier scope is externally unverifiable. Dai and Stern give fixed-stratum U-test asymptotics, and Dai, Shen and Stern give propensity-reweighted observational U-test asymptotics. Those verified guarantees do not characterize \(N^*(K,\Delta,\eta)\) uniformly as \(K\) grows, certify finite-sample errors over the entire unknown-common-mean-contrast null, or give a matching all-test information bound on the prescribed class. This is a conditional priority claim, not an inference from missing text. Dukes, Stensrud, Brioschi and Hudson (2026) give structured-CATE homogeneity tests with asymptotic guarantees for continuous or discrete covariates. The accessible abstract does not establish the growing-\(K\), binary-outcome, finite-sample minimax public-width frontier \(N^*(K,\Delta,\eta)\).
fill: Derive and explicitly evaluate the full width-dependent testing complexity on \(\mathcal M_{K,\eta}\), with a total finite original-record test and legal same-class information bounds. The restriction \(\mu_{aj}\in[1/4,3/4]\) excludes rare and near-certain binary outcomes; it is disclosed rather than attributed to Zeng et al. Complete published-text priority clearance remains a publication gate.
